datatype.name: SideCount
datatype.definition: The number of straight sides (edges) bounding a polygon; at least three.

provenance.source: Euclid, Elements, Book I, Definition 19 (rectilinear figures)
provenance.ref: trilateral, quadrilateral and multilateral figures distinguished by number of sides

interface.name: IComparable
interface.definition: Contract for a totally ordered numeric value: any two values can be ranked. compareTo returns a negative integer, zero, or a positive integer according as self is less than, equal to, or greater than the other value.

concept.name: MathematicalObject
concept.definition: An abstract object of mathematics: an entity existing outside space-time and without causal powers, individuated purely by its defining properties.

provenance.source: WMOOP L0 stereotype — Abstract entity (category C): outside space-time, no causal powers.

concept.name: Collection
concept.definition: A "many-as-one": a single abstract object that gathers zero or more member objects into a whole. The L0 Collection stereotype, realised here for the mathematical collections (whose members are themselves mathematical objects).

provenance.source: WMOOP L0 stereotype — Collection (a many-as-one grouping of members).
provenance.note: The many-as-one conception follows Cantor's notion of a set as a collection gathered into a whole.

property.name: isEmpty
property.definition: Whether the collection has no members.

provenance.source: WMOOP modelling choice — a membership predicate over the collection.

relation.name: hasMember
relation.definition: A member gathered by this collection — the set-membership relation (∈), which is NOT mereological parthood (an element is not a "part" of a set).

concept.name: Set
concept.definition: A set: a collection of distinct members, unordered and without repetition, determined entirely by which objects are its members (extensionality).

provenance.source: Halmos, P. R., Naive Set Theory, Van Nostrand (1960)
provenance.ref: the concept of a set; the axiom of extension

property.name: isFinite
property.definition: Whether the set has finitely many members.

provenance.source: WMOOP modelling choice — the finite/infinite distinction as a Boolean facet.
provenance.note: Finiteness after Dedekind (a set is infinite iff it is equinumerous with a proper subset of itself); cf. Halmos, Naive Set Theory.

concept.name: Number
concept.definition: A mathematical object expressing magnitude, count, or position on the real number line. In this module "Number" ranges over the real tower (ℕ ⊂ ℤ ⊂ ℚ ⊂ ℝ), which is totally ordered — hence IComparable.

provenance.source: ISO 80000-2:2019, Quantities and units — Part 2: Mathematics
provenance.ref: standard number sets ℕ, ℤ, ℚ, ℝ

concept.name: NaturalNumber
concept.definition: A non-negative whole number 0, 1, 2, 3, … generated from zero by repeated succession (the counting numbers).

provenance.source: Peano, G. (1889), Arithmetices principia, nova methodo exposita
provenance.ref: the Peano axioms for the natural numbers

provenance.source: ISO 80000-2:2019, Quantities and units — Part 2: Mathematics
provenance.ref: the set of natural numbers ℕ

concept.name: Integer
concept.definition: A whole number — zero, a positive natural number, or its negative (…, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, …). The naturals embed in the integers (ℕ ⊂ ℤ).

provenance.source: ISO 80000-2:2019, Quantities and units — Part 2: Mathematics

concept.name: RationalNumber
concept.definition: A number expressible as a ratio p/q of two integers with q ≠ 0, identified up to equality of ratios. The integers embed in the rationals (ℤ ⊂ ℚ).

provenance.source: ISO 80000-2:2019, Quantities and units — Part 2: Mathematics
provenance.ref: the set of rational numbers ℚ

concept.name: RealNumber
concept.definition: A number on the continuous number line: a member of the unique complete totally ordered field, containing the rationals and their limits (ℚ ⊂ ℝ).

provenance.source: ISO 80000-2:2019, Quantities and units — Part 2: Mathematics
provenance.ref: the set of real numbers ℝ

concept.name: GeometricShape
concept.definition: An abstract geometric figure: that which is contained by one or more boundaries, studied up to its defining properties rather than any physical drawing of it.

provenance.source: Euclid, Elements, Book I, Definition 14
provenance.ref: a figure is that which is contained by any boundary or boundaries

concept.name: Polygon
concept.definition: A plane figure bounded by a finite number of straight line segments (sides) joined end to end to form a single closed chain.

provenance.source: Euclid, Elements, Book I, Definition 19 (rectilinear figures)

property.name: sideCount
property.definition: The number of straight sides bounding the polygon (equal to its number of vertices).

provenance.source: Euclid, Elements, Book I, Definition 19 (rectilinear figures)
provenance.ref: trilateral, quadrilateral and multilateral figures distinguished by number of sides

property.name: isRegular
property.definition: Whether the polygon is both equilateral (all sides equal) and equiangular (all interior angles equal).

provenance.source: WMOOP modelling choice — regularity as a Boolean facet (equilateral and equiangular).

invariant.message: A polygon has at least three sides.

concept.name: Triangle
concept.definition: A three-sided polygon (trilateral). Its three interior angles sum to two right angles (π rad).

provenance.source: Euclid, Elements, Book I, Definition 19 (trilateral figures)
provenance.note: The interior-angle sum of two right angles is Elements, Book I, Proposition 32.

invariant.message: A triangle has exactly three sides.

concept.name: Quadrilateral
concept.definition: A four-sided polygon (quadrilateral). Its four interior angles sum to four right angles (2π rad).

provenance.source: Euclid, Elements, Book I, Definition 19 (quadrilateral figures)
provenance.note: Elements, Book I, Definition 22 names the square, oblong, rhombus and rhomboid quadrilaterals.

invariant.message: A quadrilateral has exactly four sides.

concept.name: AlgebraicStructure
concept.definition: A set (the carrier) together with one or more operations on it that satisfy a fixed list of axioms. Concrete structures (groups, rings, fields, …) differ by their operations and the axioms those operations obey.

provenance.source: Standard abstract algebra — an algebraic structure is a carrier set with operations satisfying stated axioms.
provenance.note: Umbrella modelling concept; cf. Dummit & Foote, Abstract Algebra, 3rd ed. (2004), Part I.

relation.name: underlyingSet
relation.definition: The carrier set of elements on which the structure's operation(s) act.

concept.name: Group
concept.definition: An algebraic structure (G, ·): a set G with a single binary operation · that is closed, associative, has an identity element, and gives every element an inverse. Below, `·` denotes the group's binary operation and the four group axioms are stated as invariants (this is the "axioms are invariants" case).

provenance.source: Dummit, D. S. & Foote, R. M., Abstract Algebra, 3rd ed., John Wiley & Sons (2004)

property.name: order
property.definition: The order of the group — the number of elements in a finite group; omitted for an infinite group.

provenance.source: Dummit, D. S. & Foote, R. M., Abstract Algebra, 3rd ed. (2004)

property.name: isAbelian
property.definition: Whether the group's binary operation is commutative (a · b = b · a for all a, b).

provenance.source: Dummit, D. S. & Foote, R. M., Abstract Algebra, 3rd ed. (2004)
provenance.ref: §1.1, abelian (commutative) group — after N. H. Abel

invariant.expr: forall a, b in self.underlyingSet: (a · b) in self.underlyingSet
invariant.message: Closure: the group is closed under its binary operation.

invariant.expr: forall a, b, c in self.underlyingSet: (a · b) · c == a · (b · c)
invariant.message: Associativity: the binary operation is associative.

invariant.expr: exists e in self.underlyingSet: forall a in self.underlyingSet: (e · a == a) and (a · e == a)
invariant.message: Identity: there is an identity element e with e · a = a · e = a.

invariant.expr: forall a in self.underlyingSet: exists b in self.underlyingSet: (a · b == e) and (b · a == e)
invariant.message: Inverse: every element a has an inverse b with a · b = b · a = e.

individual.name: EmptySet
individual.definition: The unique set with no members (∅); it is empty and finite.

provenance.source: ISO 80000-2:2019, Quantities and units — Part 2: Mathematics

individual.name: TrivialGroup
individual.definition: The trivial group ({e}, ·): the one-element group whose only element is the identity; it is abelian and has order 1.

provenance.source: Dummit, D. S. & Foote, R. M., Abstract Algebra, 3rd ed. (2004)
